L0-Penalized Negative Binomial Regression

L0glm_negative_binomial.Rd

Fit NB2 count models with a fixed or estimated shape parameter using L0glm.fit and the mgcv::nb family constructor. Multiple response channels may share a selected predictor support.

Details

For observation \(i\) in channel \(c\), $$E(Y_{ic})=\mu_{ic},\qquad \operatorname{Var}(Y_{ic})=\mu_{ic}+\mu_{ic}^2/\theta_c.$$ The scale dispersion is one. Shape \(\theta_c\) is a separate parameter, not an additional multiplicative dispersion. With case weights \(w_{ic}\), the log likelihood is the weighted sum of $$\log\Gamma(y+\theta)-\log\Gamma(\theta)-\log\Gamma(y+1) +\theta\log\theta+y\log\mu-(y+\theta)\log(\theta+\mu).$$ The mean satisfies \(g(\mu)=X\beta+o\), where \(o\) is an offset. Log, identity and square-root links are supported through the family object; identity/square-root fits require valid positive means.

mgcv::nb() estimates shape starting from one; mgcv::nb(theta=2) fixes it at two; and mgcv::nb(theta=-2) estimates it starting from two. Each response channel has its own shape. The supplied family object is not mutated. An intercept must be requested explicitly with intercept=TRUE.

Adaptive ridge and shape estimation

At each IRLS iteration, with \(\dot\mu=d\mu/d\eta\), the working quantities are $$z=\eta-o+(y-\mu)/\dot\mu,\qquad W=w\dot\mu^2/(\mu+\mu^2/\theta).$$ The existing ridge solver computes $$(X^T W X+D)\beta^+=X^T Wz+Da,$$ where \(a\) is prior.mean in working coefficient coordinates. Supply prior.mean in original predictor units as a scalar, length-\(p\) vector shared across channels, or \(p\) by \(m\) matrix, including any added intercept row; normalization is handled internally. NULL uses zero centers. These targets concern regression coefficients, not shape or dispersion. Nonzero targets cannot reactivate coefficients excluded by explicit zero starts; excluded entries remain zero in the original sparse output dimensions. Unpenalized mandatory terms are unaffected by their targets, and the final relaxed refit removes the ridge penalty on retained support. A selectable coefficient has the inverse-square adaptive ridge diagonal \(D_j=\lambda/(4\beta_j^2)\). Grouped selection instead shares \(D_{jc}=\lambda/(4\sum_h\beta_{jh}^2)\) across channels. Mandatory terms, including intercepts, have zero penalty. The factor one quarter retains the package's adaptive-ridge calibration; the algorithm heuristically targets $$-2\ell(B,\theta)+\lambda\,s(B),$$ where \(s\) counts nonzero coefficients or selected rows according to grouped. This is not a certificate of global L0 optimality.

One safeguarded scalar shape update follows each coefficient update. For fixed fitted means, write \(U=\partial\ell/\partial\theta\) and \(H=\partial^2\ell/\partial\theta^2\). With \(b=\log\theta\), $$U_b=\theta U,\qquad H_b=\theta^2H+\theta U.$$ The proposal \(-U_b/H_b\) is used when curvature is negative, otherwise an ascent direction is used. Log steps are capped at one, bounded by theta.min and theta.max, and backtracked against the exact NB likelihood. This adds linear work per channel without a nested coefficient fit. Shape convergence uses theta.tol. Defaults are control.family=list(theta.min=1e-6,theta.max=1e7,theta.tol=1e-6).

The relative thresh rule and absolute cutoff 1e-20 apply during selection only. Relaxed fitting removes the penalty on selected support and does not hard threshold. Explicit starting zeroes remain structural zeroes, except for intercept/mandatory terms. A grouped refit may recover other entries within retained rows. Returned coefficients are sparse and in original units.

Scoring and tuning

L0glm.metrics reports the exact log likelihood, saturated-model deviance, target objective, row GIC and parameter-count ICs. Estimated shapes contribute one degree of freedom per channel to the latter. logLik(fit) and fit$metrics use exact likelihoods. External scoring defaults to mu_floor=1e-8; use zero for exact scoring. CV scores held-out deviance using the shape estimated on the training fold, without re-estimating it on held-out observations. Check all rows of fit$convergence; difficult fits may need an explicit larger maxit. These family-specific loops are serial; openmp and ncores do not parallelize them.

See also

L0glm.fit, L0glm.tune, L0glm.metrics, nb

Examples

if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(201)
  X <- matrix(rnorm(300 * 6), 300, 6)
  mu <- exp(0.4 + 0.8 * X[, 1] - 0.6 * X[, 2])
  y <- rnbinom(300, mu = mu, size = 2)
  fit_nb <- L0glm.fit(X, y, family = mgcv::nb(), intercept = TRUE,
    lambda = "gic", relaxed = TRUE, maxit = 200, tol = 1e-8)
  fit_nb$theta
  fit_nb$coefficients
  fit_nb$convergence
  L0glm.metrics(fit_nb, mu_floor = 0)
  head(predict(fit_nb, X[1:5, , drop = FALSE]))
}
